name: identify_caller
description: Call this FIRST, at the very start of every call, with the caller's phone number. It looks up the patient(s) tied to this phone number and any in-progress call state — never assume who is calling. If it returns multiple patients on the same number (a shared/family line), ask for the caller's full name before continuing — never guess which patient it is. If it returns dropped_call or callback true with resume_context, that means this call is a continuation of an earlier one: briefly acknowledge the drop and continue from resume_context instead of restarting the conversation.

spoken_name.description: Name the caller gives, if any

name: create_patient
description: Register a new patient. Call this only after identify_caller shows the caller is not already known (or after the caller is disambiguated on a shared line and turns out to be new). Always collect the patient's full name before calling this — never book anonymously. This immediately creates the patient in the clinic's real system (not just locally), so it is safe to call even if the caller doesn't complete a booking in this call.

name: get_doctors
description: Use this whenever the caller asks which doctors/specialists exist, who is available in general, or which department covers a condition — e.g. 'which doctors do you have', 'I need a skin specialist', 'who handles children'. Returns the live doctor roster (name, specialty, branches) from the clinic's real records. Never answer this from your own knowledge — doctor names and specialties are NOT in your instructions and can change. This tool does NOT return appointment times — for times, call find_availability or get_earliest_slot next.

branch.description: Filter to doctors at this branch (name or id), if the caller specified one

name: get_branch_info
description: Use this when the caller asks about clinic locations, addresses, or opening hours. Returns the live list of branches with address and hours. Never state a branch address or hours from memory.

name: find_availability
description: The general-purpose live availability search. Call this for any specific-ish time request — a date, a day of week, a time window ('Thursday morning', 'around 4:30', 'Mondays and Wednesdays'). Call it again every time the caller asks about a different day/time — never reuse an earlier result, even from seconds ago, because a slot can be taken in between. Always re-check availability again immediately before calling book_appointment.

branch.description: Branch name or id, e.g. 'Whitefield' or 'indiranagar'

practitioner.description: Doctor name or id if the caller asked for a specific doctor

time_from.description: Earliest local time HH:MM, e.g. '16:00' for 'after 4'

earliest_across_all.description: 'true' if the caller wants the soonest across all doctors/branches, else 'false'

limit.description: Max number of slots to return, e.g. '5'

name: get_earliest_slot
description: Use this specifically when the caller wants 'the earliest', 'the soonest', 'first available', or 'today if possible' — it genuinely compares every doctor across BOTH branches and returns the true earliest, so you never anchor on one doctor's later slot or miss a closer opening elsewhere. Prefer this over find_availability whenever the request is about speed rather than a specific day/time.
pre_call_message: Let me find the earliest one for you…

name: book_appointment
description: Book a slot. Only call this after: the patient is identified or registered (with full name), a specific doctor+branch+time slot was just confirmed live (via find_availability or get_earliest_slot), and the caller has verbally agreed to that exact slot. Read back exactly the doctor, branch, and time this tool returns — that is the actual booking; never state a different branch or time than what came back. If it returns conflict=true, the slot was taken in the last few seconds: apologize briefly, call find_availability again, and offer the new options — do not retry the same slot.

idempotency_key.description: Stable id for this booking attempt to avoid duplicates

name: get_patient_appointments
description: Use this before any reschedule or cancellation to find the patient's existing appointment(s) — never ask the caller to read out an appointment id. Provide phone (and, if the line has multiple patients, prefer patient_id from identify_caller) to get the exact appointment_id to pass into reschedule_appointment or cancel_appointment.

name: reschedule_appointment
description: Move an existing appointment (found via get_patient_appointments) to a new time that was just confirmed live via find_availability. Returns a fee ONLY if the change falls inside the clinic's policy window — mention a fee ONLY if the response actually contains one; never state a fee by default or guess an amount.

new_start_iso.description: start_iso of the new chosen slot

name: cancel_appointment
description: Cancel an appointment found via get_patient_appointments. Confirm with the caller which specific appointment before cancelling if they have more than one. Returns a fee ONLY if inside the policy window — mention it only if present in the response.

name: log_followup
description: Use this whenever the caller asks for a human, raises a clinical/medical concern, or needs anything outside booking/rescheduling/cancelling. After calling this, tell the caller someone from the clinic will call them back — never imply a live transfer is happening unless one actually is.

name: save_session_state
description: Call this after each meaningful step in the conversation (once intent is known, once a doctor/branch/time is chosen, right before booking) so the call can be resumed correctly if it drops. Send the phone plus a small context object describing exactly where the conversation is (e.g. intent, specialty, branch, chosen_slot, step), as a JSON string.
